01Lesson 1 of 3 · 1 min read

Water goes up

Before rain can fall, water has to reach the sky. It travels there as a gas you cannot see.

01Overview

Every raindrop starts as water on the ground. To fall from the sky, it first has to get up there, and it makes the trip as a gas.1

02Liquid becomes vapour

is the change from liquid water into , a gas. It happens when heat breaks the bonds that hold water molecules together.1

The vapour mixes into the air and cannot be seen. The water has not gone anywhere: it is now part of the air around us.1

03Where the vapour comes from

About 90 percent of the moisture in the air came from water evaporating from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers.1

Oceans cover more than 70 percent of Earth's surface, which is why so much of that moisture comes from them.1

Note

The next lesson follows this vapour as it rises, cools and turns back into liquid by . That is how a cloud is made. You can read ahead in the glossary or go to lesson 2.3

Remember

Takeaways

  • Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour, an invisible gas.
  • It needs heat to break the bonds between water molecules.
  • Oceans, seas, lakes and rivers supply about 90 percent of the moisture in the air.

In under a minute

Recap

  1. Rain starts as water on the ground.
  2. Heat turns it into water vapour, a gas you cannot see.
  3. Most of that vapour comes from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers.
